headline: Showers end this evening and fog is likely for the Monday morning commute, then a warm Monday (70s in the Piedmont) gives way to a cooler week, with rain likely Wednesday into Thanksgiving Day and a period of heavy rain possible Wednesday night.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Drizzle and light showers around Charlotte and much of the area taper off from southwest to northeast through Sunday afternoon and evening as a low off the Carolina coast moves north, though low clouds hang on overnight. With moist air and light winds, fog is likely to become widespread toward dawn Monday; forecasters aren't yet sure it will be widely dense, but drivers should expect locally dense fog during the Monday morning commute, slow down and leave extra space.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Fog and clouds clear from the foothills and Piedmont Monday morning, and highs reach the 70s across most of the Piedmont, including Charlotte — about 10 degrees above normal — with a few sprinkles possible in the afternoon ahead of a cold front; along the North Carolina–Tennessee border, clouds and scattered showers persist much of the day with temperatures similar to Sunday. Mountain showers fade Monday evening, and cooler air brings Tuesday highs slightly below normal under strong high pressure, with Wednesday morning lows a little below normal.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Rain becomes likely Wednesday as cool air stays wedged against the mountains while moist air rides over it, making Wednesday the coolest day of the week with highs mainly in the upper 40s to low 50s (colder if rain starts early); it should be all rain except perhaps brief snow or sleet with little or no accumulation above about 6,000 feet. Rain chances peak above 75% for nearly the whole area late Wednesday night into early Thanksgiving morning, when moisture runs near twice normal and a period of heavy rain looks likely, though chances of 1 inch in 6 hours or 2 inches in 24 hours are low for now and the flood risk looks low. Rain tapers from southwest to northeast on Thanksgiving Day with highs near normal in the Piedmont; a little light snow or rime ice is possible along the Tennessee border Thursday night without meaningful accumulation, and Friday and Saturday look dry with near-normal temperatures.

watch_for: Locally dense fog for the Monday morning commute.
Rain amounts Wednesday night into Thanksgiving morning — heavy rain is likely for a time, and the low flood risk could rise as more detailed models come in.
confidence: Forecasters are fairly confident in showers ending tonight, a warm Monday and a cooler Tuesday, and confidence is increasing in rain Wednesday into early Thursday, though how heavy it gets and whether dense fog becomes widespread Monday morning are still uncertain.
